verdict.rationale: Gmail's own docs say offline mode lets you read, search, and reply without a connection. Messages sent offline wait in an Outbox and send automatically when you reconnect, so the core of the story is first-party documented. However, only outgoing mail is documented to sync; other offline changes are not. Missing for 10: documented sync of other offline mailbox changes (labels, archive/delete, read status) on reconnect, explicit coverage of composing brand-new messages rather than only replies, and independent or hands-on corroboration of offline reliability.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can read, search, and write email offline, with changes syncing when I reconnect

citations.quote: You can use Gmail offline to read, search, and reply to messages without an internet connection.
If you send a message offline, it's saved in a new "Outbox" folder. If you connect to the internet, the message is sent automatically.
